key_developments: 3 Nov: RBA hiked 25bp to 4.85% on a 6–3 vote and dropped its further-tightening language; AUD/NZD fell 40 pips that day, and AUD fell against every G10 currency except NOK on the week.
3 Nov: US midterms delivered a Democratic sweep; on 5 Nov the Nasdaq 100 fell 6.36% and the S&P 500 4.36%, and VIX closed at 28.18 (25.64 on 6 Nov).
3 Nov: Swiss October CPI rose to 1.5% yoy against 1.3% expected, above the SNB's 1.2% Q4 forecast.
4 Nov: French National Assembly unanimously rejected the 2027 revenue budget; OAT-Bund then tightened to 148.2bp on 5 Nov.
5 Nov: BoE hiked to 4.00% with eight votes for 25bp and one for 50bp.
6 Nov: US payrolls +165,000 against 65,000 expected and unemployment 4.1%; CME FedWatch December hike probability 76.8% from 66.9%.
6 Nov: Canadian employment −4,700 against +13,600 expected and unemployment 6.7%; USD/CAD rose 135 pips on the day.
Brent fell to a $98.32 settle on 6 Nov, its steepest weekly fall since 2020, on US–Iran deal bets ($94.62 on 4 Nov).
7 Nov: NZ preliminary count gives the coalition 67 of 131 seats, one above a majority, with about 700,000 special votes outstanding.
new_risks_identified: Equity-led risk-off driven by AI and politics rather than credit: the 5 Nov crash pushed VIX to 28.18 and drove the franc and yen bid behind losses in GBP/CHF, USD/CHF and the yen-cross shorts.
Oil fell about 16% on peace bets before any settlement, eroding the energy channel behind the structural EUR and GBP shorts.
The RBA's hike landed as a peak signal, so AUD weakness is now hitting long AUD/NZD and short EUR/AUD at the same time.
The BoE delivered a unanimous hike with conditional guidance for more, challenging the over-priced-BoE thesis across all sterling shorts.
NZ special-vote count could still produce a hung parliament, with the official result around 27 Nov.
